intro: Every day the dice roll a premise and a dozen constraints, and the game has to honor all of them. Today's roll was seed 487038373. Here is each roll and what came of it.

rolls.value: a squid painter · growing · rubber ducks
rolls.became: A squid paints ducks, sure, but how do you grow a rubber duck? You squish two of them together. Sepia gets eight arms' worth of brushes, and the ducks go from Ducklet to Galleon to Leviathan and keep going.
You drag duck onto matching duck to merge them, and drag the stamp onto the forms.

rolls.value: a limited grid · a reset loop
rolls.became: The pond is the grid, and it's always too small. The reset is a Flotilla: send your whole fleet out to sea, come back famous, start over with better brushes.
So a bigger duck has to be legal first. Clerk Juniper, a crab, won't let a new size float until you stamp the right form. Form 7-B is the Application to Exceed Bath Size.
A pier needs a carnival game, so Barnaby the gull runs a hook-a-duck booth. Sometimes the prize under the duck is coins. Sometimes it's more paperwork.
A night pier, with Sepia and Juniper drawn as glowing neon tubes. Two of the upgrades are signs: “DUCKS” and “OPEN LATE.”
A chronicle of mighty deeds, applied to bath toys. “Lo, the pier is lit.” The stamp gleams with the light of a thousand approvals.
Coins stay in the hundreds. The number that runs away is the size of the duck.
Late-night pier beats for a squid working the night shift.
Sepia wants their ducks out in the world, carrying their name. Every Flotilla sends some away, and postcards come back.
So the last duck has to be big enough to ride. The Duck of Unreasonable Size is a registered vessel, and Sepia means to sail off on it.

rolls.value: one you have to be talked out of
rolls.became: The pier begs Sepia to stay. Barnaby the gull has nobody else to toss their one coin to. The Pier Committee (three herrings in a coat) made a plaque, and the plaque is a duck. Then Juniper brings out Form 1, the Application to Be Missed, and the “Will be missed?” box left blank on every form all game finally gets filled in.

outro: None of this was planned as one idea. It's twelve dice and a lot of saying yes.
